title: Lead-Safe Work Practices (EPA RRP) on Installation Jobs
content:
**Compliance standard — lead-safe work practices on Installation Jobs**

Replacing windows or doors disturbs painted surfaces, so in older homes the crew on an **Installation Jobs** record follows lead-safe work practices under the EPA Renovation, Repair and Painting rule, led by a certified renovator, with containment, cleanup and cleaning verification.

## Applicability

Lead-safe work practices and their fee apply only when the home at the service address was built before the stated year according to the customer profile. A home built in or after the stated year carries no lead-safe fee, whatever the customer asks.

The year that decides applicability is the year built recorded on the customer profile of the job's customer. The customer's own statement of the home's age does not decide it; the system record does.

## Amount

*Retired clause:* "The fee is the method's lead-safe fee per opening times the openings on the job, never less than the method's minimum per job, assessed once on the first crew day." This clause is **no longer in force** and is superseded by the current basis for the lead-safe fee.

## Applicability table (stated year 1978, hypothetical homes)

| Year built on the customer profile | Lead-safe work practices and fee |
|---|---|
| 1977 | Apply — built before the stated year |
| 1978 | Do not apply — built in the stated year |
| 1995 | Do not apply — built after the stated year |

## Points of judgement

- **A customer who asks for lead-safe practices in a newer home.** A home built in or after the stated year carries no lead-safe fee, whatever the customer asks.
- **A customer who says the home is older than the profile shows.** Applicability follows the year built according to the customer profile.
- **What the practices involve.** A certified renovator leads the work, with containment, cleanup and cleaning verification.

superseded_clauses: The fee is the method's lead-safe fee per opening times the openings on the job, never less than the method's minimum per job, assessed once on the first crew day.
